summary.text: Troy Jackson is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Maine, chosen at a July 25, 2026 party convention after Graham Platner withdrew. A fifth-generation logger from Allagash, he served in the Maine House from 2002 to 2008 and the Maine Senate from 2008 to 2014 and 2016 to 2024, including as Democratic leader and Senate president, and lost the 2026 Democratic primary for governor.

paragraphs.text: Troy Jackson describes himself as a working-class Mainer and fifth-generation logger from Allagash who spent most of his life working in the woods. He earned an associate degree from the University of Maine at Fort Kent in 2000 and has worked as a self-employed logger.
He cites the 1998 blockade, in which he stood up to powerful landowners he said were undercutting Maine workers, as the root of his politics.

Jackson served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2008. He was elected to the Maine Senate in 2008 from District 35 and served until 2014, then ran for the U.S. House in Maine's 2nd District and lost the June 10, 2014 Democratic primary to Emily Cain.

He returned to the Maine Senate in 2016, representing District 1, and served until December 3, 2024, holding the posts of Democratic leader and Senate President; he did not run for re-election in 2024.
He was a Maine superdelegate to the 2016 Democratic National Convention and was listed as supporting Bernie Sanders.
Jackson ran for governor in 2026 and lost the June 9 Democratic primary, which Hannah Pingree won.
After Platner, the winner of the June 9 Senate primary, withdrew from the general election on July 10, 2026, Jackson won the party's July 25 nominating convention to replace him.

His Ballotpedia survey lists his campaign priorities as lower costs for Maine families, including Medicare for All and lower prescription drug and electricity costs, protecting abortion rights, strengthening unions, and abolishing ICE.
